title: Regression: Shooting, Steals and Blocks
markdown:
<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** Pay for volume that holds from year to year: three-point attempts, rim contests and deflections. Do not pay for last season's percentages or steal conversion, because FT%, 3P% and steals are among the least stable numbers. During the season, three-point swings on steady attempts are the main source of buy-low and sell-high trades before the 2027-03-04 deadline.

## Volume holds, accuracy does not

Shot volume repeats well from one season to the next, but accuracy does not. Three-point attempts per game correlate at 0.88 year to year and threes made at 0.86. Three-point percentage correlates at only 0.45. Two-point percentage correlates at 0.53, true shooting at 0.52 and free throw percentage at 0.49. Free throw percentage is now the least stable standard category. Along with steals, it swings the most from year to year. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1231), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1521), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=72))

In our 9-cat league this matters more than it looks. Three-point percentage is a hidden category. It feeds 3PTM, PTS and FG%. FG% and FT% each touch two categories. Our FG% and FT% are team ratios, so a high-volume shooter whose percentage slips hurts your team number the most. A player whose fantasy value depends on elite shooting is a risky buy. ([07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=249), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=695))

Judge a player by how he shot last season, not by a fixed label like 'bad shooter'. Only extreme cases, such as Giannis at the free throw line, are close to certain. The same caution runs the other way. Do not bank on a shooting improvement. Count it as a bonus. Be especially skeptical when a non-shooter rebuilds his jumper, because one expert believes that fails more often than it works. ([07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=178), [09-14](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1745), [08-12](https://youtu.be/p9XE5jFqhvs?t=1684))

## Spotting FT%, 3P% and 2P% outliers before the auction

Free throws: unexpected swings in either direction usually drift back toward the player's norm, and you cannot predict them. Several players had big free throw drops last season for no clear reason. Treat that as a pattern that likely reverts. At the 2026-10-18 auction, project FT% at the career norm. Do not pay extra for a spike, and do not take a big discount for an unexplained drop. ([07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=2181), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1071))

Threes: a big jump in three-point percentage on the same volume should not be expected to continue. A good percentage on low volume does not make a reliable shooter either. You need about five or six attempts per game, or a high share of shots from three. Bid on attempts, which are stable, and pull the percentage back toward the career mark. ([08-13](https://youtu.be/okN3fbHJtlA?t=445), [07-26](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2167), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1521))

Twos and FG%: if a two-point percentage starts with a 7, expect it to come down. Be skeptical of 70% field goal shooters in general, and of very high percentages on both twos and threes. Outlier FG% players tend to regress, and a small drop can wipe out most of their edge. Rim finishing is higher volume and somewhat more predictable, but swings there matter more. An 11-point drop at the rim might cost about 3 points of overall FG%. Elite mid-range shooting is low volume and rarely repeats, although shot quality is player-specific. Also check the teammates. Elite passers who create shots can strongly lift a player's finishing, so look at whether that context is still there. ([07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1334), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1304), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2107), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=870), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1087), [08-14](https://youtu.be/owlM6b8oUd0?t=1086), [07-26](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2258), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1575))

Hot stretches: elite true shooting over two months usually does not stick. When a player had a run like a post All-Star surge, use the earlier part of his season as the baseline. Be skeptical of big spikes over a short stretch, such as the final 30 games, until they hold up. After an outlier shooting season on high volume, also expect the volume to drift back toward the career norm. Before you bid, ask one question. Is this player's value propped up by shooting numbers that may not hold, or does he have room to improve? ([09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=991), [08-25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=601), [08-27](https://youtu.be/ZAyie8lKyYc?t=765), [07-21](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=407), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=341))

## Steals and blocks: activity versus conversion

Steals: deflections correlate strongly with steals (0.86). But only 49% of deflections become steals, and luck decides who recovers the ball. The rate at which deflections turn into steals correlates at only 0.32 year to year. Steals are one of the most volatile categories. Do not rely on last season's steals, and do not pay for a career-high steal rate. Pay for deflection volume and treat a high conversion rate as luck. ([07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1118), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1344), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1209), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1002))

Steals also bounce back. A drop from three steals to two cuts a third of a player's value in that category, and it can return. An elite steal skill can recover after one down year. Do not value a player on a single season. A proven ball hawk coming off a down steal year is a fair target at the auction or later in a trade. ([08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1292), [09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1108), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1002))

Blocks: shots defended, especially at the rim, correlate with blocks. League average conversion of rim contests into blocks is 13.5%. Compare each player to his own career trend. Very low converters could move a couple of points toward average, which adds about 0.2 to 0.3 blocks per game. Watch for a double hit: fewer rim contests from a role or position change, plus a drop in conversion. Elite shot blockers can also lose blocks because opponents stop shooting at them. ([07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=539), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=814), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=922), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=766), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=607))

Role changes also move block rates. Players who go for more blocks commit more fouls. As players age and their minutes rise, block and foul rates tend to drop, because starters playing big minutes cannot risk foul trouble. Do not assume a bench big keeps his per-minute block rate when he moves into a big starting role. The long-term plan is to build a baseline conversion rate for each player (blocks, steals, assists) to spot those who underperformed because of luck. ([08-25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=1705), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=2159))

## Where the experts differ on blocks

The notes disagree on how far block conversion will move. One expert finds that turning rim contests into blocks is very sticky, at 0.82 year to year, far more stable than steal conversion (0.32) or assist conversion (0.27). Another says very high block conversion should regress, very low conversion should rise, and a low converter might gain 0.2 to 0.3 blocks per game. Practical middle ground: trust block conversion much more than steal conversion. Only fade a block rate that is extreme compared with the player's own career, or one that comes with fewer rim contests. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1344), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=539), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=814), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=922))

## In-season: three-point swings drive buy-low and sell-high

Most buy-low and sell-high calls come from swings in three-point percentage. A buy-low player usually has had a cold streak from three. A sell-high player has shot something like 60% from three early in the season. Check attempts first. If his three-point attempts hold steady, the percentage is the noise, because attempts are stable and accuracy is not. Hot starts built on extreme rim finishing also tend to fade. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1478), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1521), [06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1449))

Timing for our league: trades are frequent and the deadline is 2027-03-04. Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21 and end 2027-03-28. Sell hot shooters to other managers before the deadline, while their percentages still look real. Buy cold shooters with steady volume before the deadline, so the bounce back can land during the playoffs. The same applies to a strong steal player in a slump. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1478), [08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1292), [09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1108))

On waivers, FAB runs daily and we get at most 6 adds a week. Do not spend a big FAB bid on a pickup whose value rests on a hot shooting run. When you judge a breakout, use his earlier baseline and ask whether attempts, minutes or rim contests changed, or only the percentages did. ([09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=991), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=695), [08-25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=601), [06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1449))
